Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old. One day, she was playing in the garden and she saw a big green stand. She didn't know what it was but it looked cool.

Anna went over to have a closer look, and when she got to the stand, something incredible happened. The stand started to move. Anna was so excited and it was so big and green.

Anna went to get her grandparents so they could see the stand too. They came outside and were all amazed. "What is it?" asked Anna's grandmother. Anna was about to find out.

The stand opened its eyes and said, "I'm an evil witch". Anna, her grandparents, and everyone around were so scared. The witch threatened them all and said, "If you don't do as I say, I'll put a spell on you". 

So everyone in the garden had to listen to the witch's orders. Anna felt so scared, but she knew that there was nothing she could do. The witch was so powerful and green. 

The witch caused so much trouble and the garden was not the same again. Anna never forgot the evil witch and the bad ending that she caused.

Once upon a time, there was a painter who lived in a small town. Everyone thought he was amazing because he could paint beautiful pictures. One day, he decided to have a painting contest.

The painter stood in the center of the town square and called out, "Who wants to join a painting contest!"

Everyone was excited and wanted to join. But there was one little boy who did not agree. He was only three years old, so he did not know how to paint. He wanted to join, but he was afraid.

The painter smiled and said, "It's okay. You can join if you want."

The little boy smiled and agreed. He took his paintbrush and started painting. All of the townspeople watched in amazement as the little boy's picture came to life.

When the contest was over, the painter declared the little boy the winner. Everyone was in shock and clapped for his amazing painting. The little boy was so happy and he did not feel any pain now.

Little Tommy was playing with his toys in his bedroom one day, when he heard a knock on the door. He opened the door to find a famous person standing there, holding a large desk. 

"Hello Tommy," said the famous person. "I've come here to give you a desk. I thought you might like to have it in your room."

Tommy was so excited! He thanked the famous person for the desk and then asked them why they were giving him such a special gift. 

The famous person replied, "I want to encourage you to keep learning and to realize your dreams." 

Little Tommy smiled and hugged the famous person. He was so grateful for the desk and he realized that the famous person was giving him more than just a special giftâ€”they were also giving him an encouraging message. With a smile, he ran off to his bedroom to set up his new desk.

Once upon a time, there was a little parrot named Peter. Peter was a very generous parrot and always shared his food with everyone. One day he wanted to record his generous heart and share it with the world.

He flew up to the top of a tree and said, â€œI want to record my generous heart,â€ as he looked around the forest.

Suddenly, a big bird named Lucy flew up next to him. Lucy said, â€œWhy donâ€™t we make a singing record?â€

Peter thought this was a great idea. Together they sang songs about being generous and sharing with others. When they were done, they recorded the singing and flew around the forest sharing the musical record with all of their animal friends.

At the end of the day, they were both happy knowing they had shared their generous hearts with the world.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She wanted to play pretend, so she decided to pretend that she was a tide. She ran and ran around the beach, pretending to be the tide.

Then, suddenly, a seagull flew overhead, disrupting the girl's pretend play. She felt very upset and cried out, "What is that thing flying around?!".

The seagull paused and looked back at the little girl. He said, "I'm just pretending to be a flying tide, like you! We can pretend to be tides together if you want?".

The little girl paused for a second, thought about it, and then smiled. She said, "Yes please! That would be fun!".

So, the little girl and the seagull both ran and flew around the beach pretending to be flying tides. They had so much fun, they played together all day long!

Sam and Jane were playing in the park. It was a warm day and they were having fun. Suddenly, Sam saw something shining in the grass. "What is it?" he asked.

Jane said, "Let's find out." She bent down and opened her hand. Inside her hand was a shiny gold ring.

"Wow," said Sam. He reached out his finger to take it. It felt warm against his skin.

Suddenly, a woman ran up to them. "That's my ring!" she shouted. "Give it back to me at once!"

Sam and Jane were so scared, they dropped the ring and ran away. 

The woman picked up the ring and smiled cruelly. "It's too late," she said. "You'll never get it back now."

Once upon a time, there lived a fox. The fox was very friendly and always loved to share. One day, the fox was walking through the forest when he came across something very heavy. The fox wondered what it was, so he asked a nearby rabbit what it was.

The rabbit said: "That's a stone. Do you want to share it with me?"

The fox smiled and nodded. He was very happy to share the heavy stone with the rabbit. He picked up the stone and carried it to the rabbit's home. 

The rabbit said: "This stone is so heavy. I don't think I can carry it alone! Can you help me?"

The fox nodded and said: "Of course. We can share it!" 

So, the fox and the rabbit shared the heavy stone until they arrived at the rabbit's home. The rabbit smiled and thanked the fox for sharing the stone with him. The fox smiled back and said: "It was my pleasure." 

The fox and the rabbit then said goodbye and went their separate ways. From then on, the fox and the rabbit were always happy to share with each other.

Once upon a time, there were two good friends. One was a bird, and the other a squirrel. One day, the two friends decided to take a walk in the park. As they were walking, they came across something shiny on the ground. It was a silver coin. 

The squirrel reached forward to grab the coin and said, "I'm going to spend it on something cool!" 
The bird quickly said, "No, no! That is wrong. We should rest it in the bank and save it for a rainy day."

The squirrel thought for a moment, and then decided the bird was right. He couldn't resist, however, adding that the coin was too beautiful not to look at every once in a while. 

The bird agreed and so the two friends decided to save the coin and look at it from time to time. 

The moral of the story is: It's important to save for a rainy day. Don't rush to spend what you have, otherwise you will regret it later.

Once there was a little girl called Lisa. She was three years old and she loved making new friends. One day she was in the park playing with her toys, when suddenly she saw something unusual. It was a needle! The needle was very shiny. Lisa knew she shouldn't touch it, so she decided to ask an adult for help.

She went to an old man and asked, "Please, could you help me?" The old man smiled and said, "Yes, I can help. What do you need?" Lisa told him about the needel, and the old man recommended she tell her mummy. 

So Lisa ran home and found her mummy. She told her all about the needle she had seen and her mummy said, "That's not a plaything, Lisa! You must never touch one of those." Her mummy recommended she stay away from needles and the old man had saved her from harm.

One day, two children were walking in the park. One of the children called out, "Look! There is so much ice over there!" 
The other child said, "Let's cover it and make it a big slide!" 
The first child said, "That's a great idea!" 
The two children ran to the ice and started to try and cover it. They pushed and tugged, but it was too heavy. As they kept trying, the ice started to crack. 
Suddenly, there was a loud noise and the ice broke apart, and the children tumbled down. As they looked around, they saw that the ice had all broken up and gone away. The heavy ice was now gone. 
The two children looked at each other in shock and sadness. They had hoped to make a nice slide but in the end, their plan had gone wrong.

Once upon a time, there was an orange dolphin in the ocean. He loved swimming around and having adventures with his friends.

One day, he came across a big, shiny object floating in the water. He wanted to get a closer look, so he swam to it. Suddenly, the object began to move and it locked him inside!

The orange dolphin started to panic and he cried out for help. A school of fishes swam over and told him that he must look for a key to unlock the object. 

The orange dolphin searched further in the ocean and he found a small key inside a clam. He used the key to unlock the object and he was set free!

The moral of the story is that it is important never to give up when something gets in the way. If you stay positive and keep looking for solutions, you can find a way to overcome any problem.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. Jane loved numbers. She counted the clouds in the sky and the stars in the night. One day, Jane's dad gave her a special present. It was a shiny steel box.

Jane opened the box and inside was a magical surprise! It was a crystal ball. Jane was so happy and wanted to explore the magical world inside. But one important rule would not let her do that. Her dad said, "Be very obedient and only look at the ball when I say."

So Jane put the ball back in the shiny steel box and obeyed. Every day, Jane would carefully take out the steel box and count the numbers inside the crystal ball. Jane became very obedient in counting numbers and soon was a master.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a ladybug called Bob. Bob was always looking for useful things to do.

One day, Bob was walking around when he heard an odd sound. It was coming from a nearby then. He crept closer to investigate and saw a tiny caterpillar getting into trouble inside the then. "Help!" yelled the caterpillar.

Bob jumped into action. He carefully climbed into the then and then pinched the side of the then with his legs. It split open and the caterpillar crawled out to safety.

Bob and the caterpillar smiled at each other. â€œMy name is Twitch,â€ said the caterpillar.

â€œI am Bob the Ladybug,â€ Bob replied. â€œIt was very useful of you to help me get out of there,â€ said Twitch.

Bob smiled and said, â€œIt is what friends do.â€

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old, but she was very smart. Her mother took her to the library, so she could learn some new things.

When they got there, Amy's mother said, "I'm going to the cafe while you listen to the lecture."

Amy didn't want to stay, she was so restless. But mother said, "Be a good girl and listen to the lecture. I'll be back in an hour."

So Amy stayed and listened to the lecture. It was about animals and she liked it. She learned new things and couldn't wait to act them out when she got home. After the lecture, her mother was back to pick her up. 

"You did so well and I'm so proud of you," she said.

Amy smiled. She was happy to have acted like such a good girl.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Lily. One day, Lily was playing outside. She saw an interesting thing on the ground.

It was very dry and it felt strange. She picked it up and looked at it. It was so interesting that she wanted to keep it. 

So, Lily took the thing and ran home. She put the thing in her pocket and went inside.

But when she took the thing out of her pocket later, it had gotten wet! She was very sad and started to cry.

Lily's mom tried to make her feel better, but she couldn't. It was too late. The thing was ruined. 

The end.

Once there was a duck who loved solving mysteries. Everywhere she went, she tried to figure out answers to questions. But one day, she came up against a puzzling problem that she couldn't seem to solve.

The duck went to ask her friend, the clever owl, for help. "This problem seems impossible to solve," she said, honestly. "Can you help me with it?"

The wise owl sighed. "That's easy," he said. "The key is to be honest with yourself and your friends. Honesty is the best way to solve any problem. And that's the secret to solving this one, too.

The duck understood and thanked the owl for his wisdom. After that, she was able to solve her problem with the power of honesty. From then on, she made sure to use her new knowledge whenever a problem arose.

The moral of this story is to be honest with yourself and others, as it is the best way to solve problems.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly. She was only three years old but already very brave. One day, Molly decided to explore the forest near her house. As she walked, she heard a deep growl. Molly was scared as she looked up and saw a big monster.

The monster said, "Hi Molly. I'm Richie the Rich Monster. I'm stuck in this tree and I need your help to get out. Can you lift me? Please?"

Molly had the courage to help Richie the Rich Monster. She lifted him out of the tree. Richie thanked Molly for helping him.

"You showed me how to be brave. You are a very kind and special girl," Richie said.

Molly smiled as she watched Richie slowly make his way out of the forest. He waved farewell and said, "Goodbye, Molly!"

Once upon a time, a little deer named Timmy was walking in the forest. Suddenly, he saw a disgusting and slimy puddle. He didn't want to touch it and so he stepped aside. But then he heard a strange sound coming from the puddle.

"Hello," said the sound.

Timmy was very scared and he asked, "Who are you?"

The sound spoke again, "I am the slimy puddle. Please come closer so that we can talk."

Timmy shook his head and said, "No, I don't want to. It looks disgusting."

But the slimy puddle kept asking him to come closer. Finally, Timmy decided to take a few steps closer. As soon as he did, the slimy puddle grabbed him and pulled him in.

When Timmy's friends heard about what happened, they were terribly sad. Sadly, Timmy was never seen again.

Mummy was playing a puzzle with her daughter. She held up a piece that fit in the puzzle and said to her daughter, "I think this piece goes here."

The daughter smiled and replied, "It does! I can see it now." She took the piece and placed it in the puzzle.

Mummy was so proud of her and said, "You are so dependable. You make me very happy."

The daughter smiled and replied, "Thanks Mummy!" Then she kept playing with the puzzle. 

Mummy wanted to make sure her daughter had fun, so she said, "Do you need some help?"

The daughter shook her head and replied, "No, I can do it. I'm a dependable puzzle master!"

Mummy laughed and gave her daughter a hug. "You make me so proud. I love you."

The daughter smiled and replied, "I love you too, Mummy."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very small, but she was very brave. One day her parents suggested she go on a special adventure. They gave her a napkin, which was black.

Lily wanted to go right away to explore what the adventure was, but her parents told her she needed to wait until the next day. She asked them why, but they said they couldn't tell her yet.

The next day, Lily woke up excited. She grabbed the black napkin, still wondering why her parents had suggested this special adventure. She followed her parents outside into their backyard. Lily was stunned when she saw it. Her parents had built an amazing pirate ship with a bright black sail. 

Lily screamed in excitement, and her parents laughed. They had suggested the adventure because they wanted her to have the most awesome day ever. Lily had a wonderful time playing around the ship with her parents. She was thankful for the black napkin, as it reminded her of the magical day.

One day there was a yellow bird. He was always watching the mechanic working. Every morning he would fly down and sit next to the mechanic's shop. 

The mechanic spoke to him and told him to stay away from the workshop. He said, â€œI won't have any trouble if you stay away from here.â€

But the bird didn't listen. He kept coming back again and again, no matter how many times the mechanic warned him. 

One day, the mechanic was tired of warning the bird. He had enough and decided to do something about it. He grabbed a stick and hit the bird, sending it flying across the sky. The poor yellow bird never came back again. 

It was a sad ending for the bird and a lesson to us all. Everyone needs to listen to warnings or else they might end up in a bad situation.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl who loved to play games. One day, she saw a marble on the ground. It was very hard and shiny. The brave girl wanted to save it, so she put it in her pocket. 

Then, the brave girl went to play in a tree. But suddenly, she heard a loud crack. The tree was falling down! The brave girl tried to jump away, but she couldn't.

The brave girl held her pocket tight. She wanted to save the marble. But it was too late. The tree fell on her and she couldn't move.

The brave girl said goodbye to the hard marble. She couldn't save it. In the end, she was very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved exploring. Every day, she would go off and search for something new and exciting. One day, she stumbled across a reef that seemed to go on and on. 

As she crept closer, she noticed that there was something strange inside. She decided to take a closer look and soon figured out that somebody had left a puzzle inside the reef! She was so excited and determined to solve this mystery so she started trying out different combinations.

After what seemed like hours, she eventually saw it - the puzzle had been solved! But then she got the feeling that somebody was watching her. When she looked around, she saw a crab scurrying away. 

The little girl was filled with guilt. She hadn't meant to take somebody else's puzzle, but she was so excited to solve it. She turned and ran away from the reef, never to return again.

Once upon a time, there were two little friends named Max and Jack. Max was very smart and Jack was very adventurous. 
Max and Jack were walking through the park one day. Max said, â€œLetâ€™s march faster, Jack! I want to look for money!â€ 
So, Max and Jack started marching fast through the park. Everywhere they looked, all they could see was leaves and green grass. 
But then Jack shouted, â€œLook, Max! Money!â€ 
Max and Jack ran towards the money. They saw a shiny gold coin lying on the ground. 
Max smiled and said, â€œLetâ€™s march home and show this to our parents!â€ 
So, Max and Jack marched fast home, and their parents were very happy with the golden coin! Max and Jack learned that even when you march fast, you can still find something special.

Once there was a race between two powerful animals. One was a big, strong elephant and the other was a fast, silly rabbit. The elephant was sure he would win the race, he was much bigger and more powerful than the rabbit. The rabbit knew he had to try his best, so he hopped and skipped his way across the finish line.

The elephant was mad. He stopped and stamped his foot and refused to move on. He was screaming and shouting that he should have won. The rabbit tried to calm him down, but the elephant wouldn't listen. He yelled and roared louder and louder until finally he flew into a rage and charged towards the rabbit. Luckily, the rabbit was fast, and he managed to run away before the elephant could catch him.

The poor elephant was still angry and upset. He ran around the field until he was exhausted. Then he stopped and lay down on the ground. He was so tired and heartbroken that he just stayed there, never to rise again. The race between the powerful animals ended sadly, with the elephant lying there on the ground, never to race again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane who loved to observe the world. She noticed many things like the colorful flowers in her garden and the birds in the sky. One day, while observing, she noticed a big tree in her neighborâ€™s yard that was full of ripe apples. 

Jane asked her mom if she could pick the apples. Her mom agreed and said, â€œPicking the apples is an excellent job, but before you do it, I have one tip for you.â€

Jane listened carefully to her momâ€™s tip. Her mom said, â€œPick the apples from the highest branch first. That's the best way to be successful.â€ Jane remembered her momâ€™s advice, and then she started picking the apples. She picked the highest apples and was successful at it. Her neighbor even invited her for a cup of hot apple juice. 

Jane thanked her mom and said, â€œI knew your tip would help me, thank you for giving me such good advice!â€

Once there was a little girl who was very kind. She wanted to help those in need and spread happiness. Every day she would take a walk down the street and look for people to care for.

One day she saw an old man, walking with a vase. He was walking very slowly and seemed to be struggling. The little girl knew she could help him. She walked up to the man and said 'Hello, can I help you with your vase?'

The old man was very happy and said 'Yes, thank you so much!' He was relieved to be able to carry the vase with less effort.

The little girl took the vase and walked alongside the old man. She was not aware that some people who were passing by had noticed what she had done and quietly admired her for her kindness.

The little girl had learned an important lesson that day: it is important to always be kind to those around you and care for those in need. Being ignorant of the feelings of others is not the way to be.

Once upon a time there were two cubes. One cube was very boring, and it stayed in one place all day. The other cube was much more adventurous and loved to split up into smaller pieces.

One day the two cubes met up for a chat. The boring cube was very jealous of the adventurous cube and wished it could do what the other cube could do. So the adventurous cube split up into small pieces and offered to show the boring cube how to do it too. 

After a lot of practice, the boring cube was finally able to split up into small cubes like the adventurous cube. They were both so proud! 

The moral of the story is that if you're brave enough to try new things, good things can happen. You never know what you can do until you try!

Gracie and her mom were in the store together. Gracie saw the makeup and wanted to buy some. Her mom said no. She said it was too cheap and she didn't want Gracie to put it on her face.

Gracie started to cry and said, "Why won't you let me get it? I really want the makeup." Her mom sighed and said, "Because it's not good for you. It's too cheap and it wouldn't look very nice."

Gracie started to cry even harder and said, "Why don't you understand? I'll save my money and buy the best one, I promise!" Her mom shook her head and said, "This isn't about how much it costs, Gracie. You're too young to wear makeup."

Gracie couldn't believe her mom said that. She was so mad. She yelled, "No, I'm not! I'm old enough to decide for myself."

Her mom just looked at her, and Gracie could tell her mom was serious. She knew her mom meant what she said. Everything seemed to freeze for a moment. Gracie had a feeling she was not going to get the makeup.

Once upon a time, there was a calm summer day in the spring. A family of four â€“ Mom, Dad, Grandma, and a three-year-old â€“ decided to part ways and go off on their own special adventure. 

The three-year-old followed Mom and Dad into the fields, hopping and skipping along the dirt path. Everywhere they explored, the fields were so green and fresh with new life. The three-year-old was so excited about their adventure.  

Next, the family came upon the edge of a lake. They were in awe of its beauty, the calm, peaceful water, and the warm breeze that passed by. Dad pointed out to the three-year-old how the lake was full of fish, and he also highlighted a group of ducks in the distance. The three-year-old was so amazed at how perfect this moment was during the spring. 

As the three-year-old played on the shore, Dad went for a swim in the lake. To the three-year-old's surprise, he jumped right back out and started to run up the shore. It turns out that Dad disturbed a swarm of bees! The three-year-old started to laugh and chase after them.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mandy. She was three years old and wanted to play outside.

"Can I come outside, Mummy?" she asked her mum.

Mummy said, "Yes, but just for a little while, Mandy. It's cold outside - there's even some ice on the ground. So you must wrap up warm!"

So little Mandy put on her coat and boots and went outside to play. She had lots of fun running and kicking leaves for a few minutes. But then she did something silly.

Mandy tried to step on the ice. "Stupid ice! I can't break it!" she said.

Mummy rushed outside and said, "Mandy! Don't do that! You could hurt yourself on the ice! Come inside now before it's too late."

So Mandy went quietly back inside, feeling a little embarrassed. But she knew it was for her own safety and so she was happy to get inside before it was too late.

"Look, Mommy!" exclaimed three-year-old Jenny. She had found a strange knot in the garden of her home.

"That looks strange," said Mommy.

Jenny decided to replace the knot with something else. She started looking around.

Suddenly, Jenny found a loud buzzer. She picked it up and quickly put it in the place of the knot.

Mommy shook her head, but said nothing.

Jenny smiled as the buzzer made a loud noise. But then, it wouldn't stop!

Mommy shouted, "What did you do?"

Unfortunately, the buzzer just kept getting louder and louder. Eventually, Mommy had to take it away and put the knot back in its place.

And Jenny learned her lesson - not to replace things without asking first!

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Carl. He was very hungry and wanted something to eat. He looked around the house and saw a big envelope on the table. He thought maybe the envelope had something special inside, so he opened it up.

What he found inside was a measuring tape. He was so excited and smiled with joy. He grabbed the measuring tape and ran around the house, measuring everything. He measured the table, the chairs, even his bed! 

Suddenly, Carl's mom came in and saw what he was doing. She smiled at him and said, "It looks like you're measuring everything. What are you measuring for?"

Carl said, "I'm measuring to find something to eat! I'm so hungry!" 

His mom laughed and said, "Well, why don't you come into the kitchen with me and we can look for something tasty."

And so, Carl and his mom went into the kitchen and found all sorts of delicious snacks! Carl was so happy and he never forgot the envelope that contained the measuring tape.

One day, Tommy was playing outside at sunset. He could see the wide sky changing colors from blue to orange, and he was very excited. He started pointing up at the sky, saying "Look! The sunset is so beautiful!"

Suddenly, his mom came outside. She smiled at Tommy and said, "You're right! It's a gorgeous sunset. I wish we could stay here and watch it together."

Tommy's dad came outside too and looked up. He pointed to the sky and said, "Wow! Look at how wide it is!"

Tommy ran up and hugged his mom and dad. He was so happy they were all looking at the sunset together. They were a family, and nothing was better than that!

Bob was a proud little boy. He was always excited to show off his new skills. Today he was learning something really special - how to use a knife.

He watched his mom as she showed him how to hold the knife and how to be very careful.

Then it was time to practice. He took the knife and cut something very carefully. He looked around and saw a bag of popcorn. He was proud of himself as he cut the popcorn into small pieces.

Bob was feeling so proud of himself. He had done it! He had used a knife to cut something all by himself. And now it was time to eat the popcorn!

Bob grabbed the bowl of popcorn and carefully nibbled on the pieces. They were nice and crunchy, just the way he liked it.

Bob smiled with satisfaction - he had just learned to use a knife, and he was proud of it!

In the park, there was a young boy named Tommy. Tommy was restless and he kept running around the big trees. His father said, "Tommy, we are going to the hospital." Tommy was scared and he asked, "Why are we going to the hospital?". His father replied, "We are going to visit your grandpa. He has been feeling very unwell." 

When they arrived at the hospital, Tommy was still restless. He kept running around the chairs and scanning the room. His father said, "Let's go and see grandpa now." Tommy was still scared but he wanted to see grandpa. 

When they got to the room, Tommy said, "Hi grandpa!" Grandpa replied, "Hello Tommy, it's great to see you!" Tommy asked, "Are you feeling better?". Grandpa said, "I'm getting better every day. But I'm still a bit tired. Would you like to sit and rest with me?" 

Tommy was happy. He sat down on the bed and asked his grandpa about what he did in the hospital. Grandpa told Tommy about how he was getting better, and how he took lots of walks around the hospital. Tommy then asked, "Can I come too?". Grandpa smiled and said, "That sounds like a wonderful idea." 

Tommy and his grandpa took a walk around the hospital together. Tommy was finally feeling restful,

Once upon a time, there was a foolish boy who wanted to fly a helicopter. He set about building one. He collected some pieces and tried to piece them together. But he couldn't make it work. 

He kept trying and eventually the foolish boy thought he'd made it work. So he set off to fly the helicopter. But it still wasn't working! He flew too high up into the sky. 

The foolish boy was stuck and he couldn't get down. After a while, he ran out of energy and tumbled to the ground. He wasn't hurt, but he was stuck there. Nobody could help him get back up. 

The foolish boy learned his lesson and he never tried to fly a helicopter again.

Once, there was a little girl called Emily. She was three years old. Every night, Emily's mum would close her door and say good night. Emily didn't like it. Every time, she wanted mum to stay in her room with her.

One night, Emily cried until her mum promised to stay with her. So, mum closed the bedroom door and sat on her bed. They both looked out of the window at the night sky.

Suddenly, the darkness was filled with a deep, sad silence. Emily was confused and a bit scared. She asked her mum, "What's wrong? Why is silences so sad?"

Mum explained that sometimes, even adults need a bit of a hug when it's quiet. Mum hugged Emily and spoke softly, "The silence will pass soon, and there will be happy noises again. It's OK."

Emily felt better and smiled. She closed her eyes and soon fell asleep in her mum's warm arms.

One day, a young boy and his mother were walking in the park. They noticed a strange station with a sign that said "Come and study!". The boy was curious, so he asked his mother what it was. She explained that people went to the station to learn things.

The boy wanted to go and study, but his mother said he was too young. The boy got upset and began to cry.

Suddenly, a stranger appeared and said, "There's no need for tears. If the boy really wants to learn, I know of a special place where he can study!"

The mother was hesitant, but the boy was excited. They thanked the stranger and went on their way.

At the end of the day, the boy was tired but a little bit smarter. He had studied at the special station and learnt all kinds of new things. He was proud of himself and promised to keep studying in the future.

Timmy was always so excited for naptime. He ran quickly to his bedroom and began to sort through his stuffed animals. One was a big and fluffy teddy bear and the other was a small and soft puppy. He couldn't decide which one he wanted to cuddle, so he asked his mom.

â€œMom, which should I pick?â€

She smiled and said, â€œThatâ€™s for you to decide.â€

Timmy looked at both of them and knew the one he wanted.

â€œIâ€™ll take the teddy bear!â€

His mom said, â€œThatâ€™s a great choice, honey.â€

After choosing his favorite toy, he noticed something strange. As he held the teddy bear, a small tire rolled out of its tummy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and have fun with her friends. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to start planting a garden. Lily was so excited because she loved flowers and vegetables.

Before they could start planting, Lily's mom said they needed to wash their hands. Washing hands is important to stay clean and healthy. Lily was a little sad because she wanted to start planting right away, but she knew it was important to wash her hands first.

After they washed their hands, Lily and her mom started planting the seeds. They dug little holes and put the seeds inside. Lily was so happy because she knew that soon they would have beautiful flowers and yummy vegetables to eat.

Days went by and Lily and her mom watered the garden every day. One day, Lily noticed something growing in the ground. It was a tiny, green sprout! Lily was so excited because she knew that soon it would turn into a big, beautiful flower. All of their hard work had paid off!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved music and would always listen to it on his little radio. One day, Timmy's mom told him to clean his room. Timmy was very clumsy and knocked over his radio while cleaning. It broke into a million pieces and Timmy was very sad.

Timmy's mom asked him what happened and Timmy told her that he was trying to clean his room but he was too clumsy and broke his radio. His mom tried to fix it but it was too broken. Timmy was very upset because he loved listening to music on his radio.

From that day on, Timmy learned to be more careful and not be so clumsy. He also learned that sometimes accidents happen and it's important to be careful with the things you love. Although Timmy was sad about his broken radio, he knew that he would always have music in his heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a pack of gum that he loved very much. He would take a piece of gum out of the pack every day and chew it. One day, Timmy went to the park to play. He saw a little girl who looked very lonely. She didn't have any friends to play with.

Timmy felt sad for the little girl, so he decided to share his gum with her. He took a piece of gum out of his pack and gave it to her. The little girl was so happy and thanked Timmy. They became friends and played together for the rest of the day. Timmy was happy that he could make someone else happy by sharing his gum.

Once upon a time, there was a poor boy named Timmy. He lived in a small house in the east part of town. Timmy's mom had to work hard every day to manage their money and buy food for them to eat.

One day, Timmy and his mom went for a walk in the park. They saw some kids playing with a ball and Timmy wanted to join in. He asked his mom if they could buy a ball, but she said they couldn't afford it. Timmy felt sad, but his mom told him they could still have fun without a ball.

They started to play a game of tag and Timmy managed to catch his mom. They both laughed and had a great time. Timmy realized that even though they were poor, they could still have fun and enjoy each other's company.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to perform a special task. She had to put all the dirty dishes in the dishwasher. Lily was very happy to help, but she found it hard to reach the top shelf. 

"Mommy, it's too hard," Lily said. 

"Don't worry, sweetie. I'll help you," her mommy replied. 

Together, they put all the dishes in the dishwasher. Lily was so proud of herself for helping. But then, something bad happened. When they turned on the dishwasher, it made a loud noise and started to shake. Suddenly, the dishwasher exploded and water went everywhere. 

Lily and her mommy were very scared and wet. They hugged each other and cried. "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't mean to do it," Lily said. 

"It's okay, sweetie. We're just glad we're safe," her mommy replied. 

From that day on, they never used the dishwasher again. They washed their dishes by hand and Lily always helped.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a dream that a fierce dragon was chasing her. She woke up and told her mommy about her nightmare. 

"I hope the dragon won't come back," said Lily.

"Don't worry, sweetie. Dragons aren't real," said her mommy.

But that night, Lily had the same nightmare again. This time, the dragon caught her and took her away. Lily never woke up.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars all day long. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to clean his room. Timmy didn't want to clean his room because he was having so much fun playing with his cars.

Timmy's mom said, "If you clean your room, you will have success and be happy." Timmy didn't understand what success meant, but he knew he wanted to be happy. So, he started cleaning his room. While he was cleaning, he accidentally knocked over his toy castle and destroyed it. Timmy felt sad because he loved his castle, but his mom said, "Don't worry, Timmy. You can always build a new one."

Timmy felt better and continued cleaning his room. When he was finished, he felt proud of himself and showed his mom. She said, "You did a great job, Timmy! You are so brave for cleaning your room even though you didn't want to." Timmy smiled and felt happy knowing he had success and made his mom proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved sweets, especially lollipops. One day, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy some candy. Lily saw a big, red lollipop and asked her mom if she could have it. 

"Can I have that lollipop, please?" Lily asked her mom.

"Of course, you can have it!" her mom replied. 

As they were walking home, Lily saw a spider crawling on the sidewalk. She was scared and didn't want to step on it. 

"Mommy, there's a spider! Can we go around it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, let's go around it so we don't hurt it," her mom said. 

Finally, they arrived home and Lily happily enjoyed her sweet lollipop.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He played on the swings and went down the slide. 

After a while, Tim's tummy started to rumble. He was hungry! His mom said they could go get some crackers to eat. They walked to the store and Tim helped his mom pick out some tough crackers. 

On the way back to the park, Tim saw a big crack in the sidewalk. He wanted to show his mom, so he ran over to it. His mom followed him and they looked at the crack together. Tim thought it was cool how the crack went all the way down to the dirt. 

Finally, they made it back to the park and Tim and his mom sat on a bench to eat their crackers. Tim was happy because he got to bring the crackers to the park and he found a cool crack in the sidewalk. It was a great day!

Once upon a time, there was a panda named Pandy. Pandy was very successful at climbing trees and eating bamboo. One day, Pandy met a rabbit named Rolly.

"Hi Pandy, do you want to play with me?" asked Rolly.

"Yes, let's play!" said Pandy.

They played hide and seek, but when it was Pandy's turn to hide, she accidentally zipped herself inside a backpack. Rolly couldn't find her and went home without her.

Pandy tried to get out of the backpack, but she couldn't. She was stuck inside and couldn't breathe. Sadly, Pandy passed away inside the backpack.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he went to the park to play with his friend, Sammy. They were having a great time until Timmy's favorite toy car got stuck in the mud. He tried to pull it out, but it wouldn't budge.

Sammy said, "Let's ask the big kids for help!"

Timmy replied, "No, they always make fun of me because I'm little."

Sammy said, "Don't worry, I'll go ask them for you."

Sammy went over to the big kids and said, "Can you help my friend Timmy? His toy car is stuck in the mud."

The big kids said, "Sure, we'll help him."

Timmy was surprised and happy that the big kids helped him. He surrendered his toy car to them and they pulled it out of the mud. Timmy thanked them and they all played together. The gloomy feeling Timmy had before was gone and he had a great day with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her aunt very much because she was very kind and always gave her gifts. One day, Lily and her aunt went for a walk in the park. While they were walking, they saw a little bird that was stuck in a tree. 

Lily said, "Aunt, we need to save the bird!" 

Her aunt replied, "You're right, Lily. We need to help the bird." 

Lily's aunt was very gifted and knew how to climb trees. She climbed up the tree and saved the bird. The bird was very happy and flew away. Lily was very proud of her aunt and said, "Aunt, you're the best!" 

Her aunt replied, "No, Lily, you're the best. You always remind me to help others." 

Lily and her aunt continued their walk in the park, feeling happy and proud of themselves for saving the little bird.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to soar high in the sky and sing happy songs. One day, Tweety saw a shiny object on top of a tall stair. Tweety wanted to see what it was, so she flew up to the top of the stair. But when Tweety got there, she saw a noisy cat waiting for her!

Tweety tried to fly away, but the cat was too fast. The cat chased Tweety around and around, trying to catch her. Tweety was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, Tweety had an idea. She flew up high into the sky and then dove down fast, right past the cat. The cat was so surprised that he fell down the stair and ran away.

Tweety was safe and happy once again. She flew back up into the sky and sang a happy song, grateful to be free from the noisy cat. From that day on, Tweety knew to be careful when exploring new places.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her stuff toys and reading books. One day, Lily's mom asked her if she dared to try a new food for dinner. Lily felt a little scared but she wanted to be brave, so she said yes.

At dinner time, Lily tried the new food and found out it was yummy! She felt proud that she was brave enough to try something new. After dinner, Lily cuddled up in her comfortable bed with her favorite stuff toy and read a book.

As she read, she realized that trying new things can be scary but it can also be fun. She felt happy that she dared to try something new and promised herself to try new things more often. From that day on, Lily felt more confident and excited to try new stuff.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play baseball with his friends. One day, Timmy's coach asked him to test his pitching skills. Timmy was nervous but he tried his best.

During the game, Timmy pitched the ball and it went too high. His friends started to laugh at him. Timmy felt sad and wanted to quit playing baseball forever. But his coach told him that everyone makes mistakes and that he should keep practicing.

Timmy listened to his coach and kept practicing. He worked hard and soon became a great pitcher. His friends were happy for him and they all played together again. The moral of the story is that it's okay to make mistakes, as long as you keep trying and practicing, you can become very good at something.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy brought home a new puppy named Max. Lily was so happy to welcome Max into their family. Max was so cute and playful!

One morning, Lily's daddy brought in the newspaper. Lily loved looking at the pictures in the newspaper. But when she tried to touch it, she accidentally tore a page. Her mommy told her that she shouldn't touch the newspaper because it's delicate.

Later that day, Lily's mommy made her favorite cookies. But Lily was being naughty and didn't finish her dinner. Her mommy told her that she couldn't have any cookies because she spoiled her dinner. Lily was sad but she knew she needed to listen to her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. One day, he found a colorful ball. He was so happy to have found it.

Timmy's mom called him inside for lunch. She made him a sandwich and gave him a glass of milk. "Mommy, can I bury my ball in the backyard?" Timmy asked.

His mom said, "Why do you want to bury your ball?"

Timmy replied, "I want to bury it so I can find it later and play with it again."

His mom smiled and said, "Okay, but make sure you remember where you bury it." So, Timmy went outside and buried his colorful ball in the backyard. He couldn't wait to dig it up and play with it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to dig in the dirt and play with his trucks. One day, while he was digging, he found a secret hole in the ground. He crawled inside and found himself in an underground cave. 

In the cave, Timmy found a treasure chest. He opened the chest and inside was a famous toy that he had always wanted. He was so happy! He couldn't wait to show his friends. 

When Timmy got home, he couldn't keep the secret anymore. He revealed to his friends that he had found a treasure chest underground and inside was a famous toy. His friends were so excited and they all went back to the cave to see it. They couldn't believe their eyes! It was the best day ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to help her mommy cook dinner. One day, Lily's mommy was making rice for dinner. She put the rice on the stove to cook. 

Lily was curious and wanted to see what was happening to the rice. She got too close to the stove and accidentally touched the hot pot. It burned her little finger! 

But don't worry, it was a harmless burn. Lily's mommy put some cold water on her finger and gave her a hug. From that day on, Lily knew to be careful around the stove when her mommy was cooking.

Once upon a time, there was a long pumpkin. The pumpkin was so long that it reached the sky. One day, a little girl walked by and saw the long pumpkin. She said, "Wow, that pumpkin is so long!"

Suddenly, a naughty boy came and disturbed the pumpkin. The little girl said, "Hey, why did you do that? You shouldn't disturb things that don't belong to you."

The naughty boy said sorry and walked away. The little girl felt happy that the pumpkin was safe. She learned that it's important to respect other people's things and not disturb them. The end.
